title: Trident Improved ampalaya: Characteristics
metaDescription: Trident Improved ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Trident Improved ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety, also sold or known as Trident Improved F1 or Trident ampalaya. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor).

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Trident Improved ampalaya is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Trident Improved F1 or Trident ampalaya, this is the same ampalaya. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ampalaya variety finder](/crop-varieties/ampalaya), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ampalaya fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 45 to 50 days after transplanting (Allied sheet), the 2015 report gives 60 to 65 days after direct sowing.
**Yield:** About 30 t/ha potential (company figure quoted in Agriculture Monthly).
**Fruit:** Long, heavy, thick fleshed, glossy dark green cylinders, 37 to 40 cm and 250 to 300 g on Allied's sheet, 30 to 40 cm and 350 to 400 g in the 2015 report.
Intermediate resistance to the 'namamarako' virus that turns vines male.
Long productive life, kept growing through cool northeast monsoon weather in Isabela.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: agriculture Monthly followed an Aurora, Isabela farmer who adopted Condor Trident Improved and kept bearing through a cold spell that slowed neighbours' ampalaya, an older Trident is in the seed industry table of the ampalaya guide. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual ampalaya on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Trident Improved ampalaya

Pick by fruit: long and light green for most markets, short and dark for the bitter lovers. Hybrids yield more on a trellis, and some are bred to tolerate the downy mildew of the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Trident Improved F1 the same as Trident Improved?
items.a: Yes. Trident Improved F1 is another name for Trident Improved. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Trident Improved?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
